translationRepairs: Prince of Jian'an Liu Xiuren, Minister of Works, was placed in overall command of the punitive armies, with General of Chariots and Cavalry and Jiangzhou inspector Wang Xuemo as his deputy.
Prince of Jian'an Liu Xiuren, Minister over the Masses, was placed in overall command of the punitive armies, with General of Chariots and Cavalry and Jiangzhou inspector Wang Xuanmo as his deputy.
司徒 is Minister over the Masses (not Works, 司空); 王玄謨 is Wang Xuanmo, not Xuemo.
Wang Xuemo had not yet marched out, but the vanguard alone comprised ten armies, arriving one after another without pause.
Wang Xuanmo had not yet marched out, but the vanguard alone comprised ten armies, arriving one after another without pause.
Prince of Anlu Liu Zisui was made Minister of Works and Yangzhou inspector;
Prince of Anlu Liu Zisui was made Minister over the Masses and Yangzhou inspector;
司徒 is Minister over the Masses, not Minister of Works (司空).
Princes of Xunyang Liu Zifang and Linhai Liu Zixiang were both granted the privilege of an office equal to the Three Excellencies;
Princes of Xunyang Liu Zifang and Linhai Liu Zixu were both granted the privilege of an office equal to the Three Excellencies;
子頊 is Zixu (頊 xū), not Zixiang.
Sizhou was established at Yiyang, and Yiyang administrator Pang Mengjiao was made its inspector.
Sizhou was established at Yiyang, and Yiyang administrator Pang Mengqiu was made its inspector.
龐孟虯: 虯 is read qiú.
Pang Mengjiao also defied the court and took up arms for Xunyang.
Pang Mengqiu also defied the court and took up arms for Xunyang.
龐孟虯: 虯 is read qiú.
Mizhi's kinsman Beihai prefect Huai Gong and his nephew Shanming both took up arms for him; hearing this, Xue Suo Er abandoned the siege of Suiling and marched against Mizhi.
Mizhi's kinsman Beihai prefect Huaigong and his nephew Shanming both took up arms for him; hearing this, Xue Suo Er abandoned the siege of Suiling and marched against Mizhi.
懷恭 is the given name of a Liu clansman (族人), not surname Huai plus Gong.

The emperor summoned Kong Kai, chief administrator to the Prince of Xunyang who was also acting Kuaiji administrator, to serve as Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and sent Yu Ye, chief of staff for the western pacification, to replace him;

The emperor summoned Kong Ji, chief administrator to the Prince of Xunyang who was also acting Kuaiji administrator, to serve as Supervisor of the Household of the Heir Apparent and sent Yu Ye, chief of staff for the western pacification, to replace him;
孔覬 is Kong Ji (覬 jì); 太子詹事 is the Supervisor of the Household of the Heir Apparent, not Grand Tutor.
Zuan urged Kai: "Jiankang is feeble; you would do better to rally the five commanderies and side with Yuan Yi and Deng Wan."
Zuan urged Ji: "Jiankang is feeble; you would do better to rally the five commanderies and side with Yuan Yi and Deng Wan."
凱 here stands for 孔覬, Kong Ji.
Kai thereupon mobilized his forces and issued urgent proclamations declaring for Xunyang.
Ji thereupon mobilized his forces and issued urgent proclamations declaring for Xunyang.

When Yizhou inspector Xiao Huikai heard that Prince of Jin'an Liu Zixun had taken up arms, he assembled his officers and said: "Prince of Xiangdong is a son of the dynastic founder by a primary consort;
When Yizhou inspector Xiao Huikai heard that Prince of Jin'an Liu Zixun had taken up arms, he assembled his officers and said: "Prince of Xiangdong is in the zhao line of Taizu (Emperor Wen);
太祖 is the temple name of Emperor Wen, not the dynastic founder; 昭 refers to the ancestral-temple generational order.
Thereupon Xiangzhou acting administrator He Huiwen, Guangzhou inspector Yuan Tanyuan, Liangzhou inspector Liu Yuanku, and Shanyang prefect Cheng Tianzuo all declared for Zixun.
Thereupon Xiangzhou acting administrator He Huiwen, Guangzhou inspector Yuan Tanyuan, Liangzhou inspector Liu Yuanhu, and Shanyang prefect Cheng Tianzuo all declared for Zixun.
柳元怙: 怙 is read hù.
Yuanku was a cousin of Liu Yuanjing.
Yuanhu was an elder paternal cousin of Liu Yuanjing.
元怙 is Yuanhu; 從兄 is an elder paternal cousin.
Zhou Jin, prefect of Runan and Xincai, raised troops at Xuanyi for Jiankang.
Zhou Jin, prefect of Runan and Xincai, raised troops at Xuanhu for Jiankang.
Kong Xuan sent his grandson Tan Guan and others to encamp at Jiuli in Jinling; their battle array was formidable.
Kong Ji sent his grandson Tan Guan and others to encamp at Jiuli in Jinling; their battle array was formidable.
孔覬 is Kong Ji; "Kong Xuan" is a wrong reading.
Liang was a collateral descendant of Shen Huaishen.
Liang was a grandnephew of Liu Huaishen.
懷慎 is Liu Huaishen (Liang shares the Liu surname); 從孫 means grandnephew.
The emperor gave Xi the acting rank of Establishing Might general and picked elite Feathered Forest guards to accompany him.
The emperor gave Xi the acting rank of Establishing Martiality general and picked elite Feathered Forest guards to accompany him.
建武將軍 is the Establishing Martiality general; Establishing Might is 建威.

In the second month, on the jiwu new moon, Xi crossed the water to attack the commandery seat, divided his force to strike the outworks, and from high ground directed the battle as though ordering an assault from every side.

In the second month, on the jiwei new moon, Xi crossed the water to attack the commandery seat, divided his force to strike the outworks, and from high ground directed the battle as though ordering an assault from every side.
己未 is jiwei, not jiwu.
The empress dowager held court and assumed the regency, bringing in secretariat director Gao Yun, secretariat gentleman Gao Lü of Fuyang, and Jia Xiu to deliberate on great affairs of state.
The empress dowager held court and assumed the regency, bringing in secretariat director Gao Yun, secretariat gentleman Gao Lü of Yuyang, and Jia Xiu to deliberate on great affairs of state.
Xi crossed from Liupu, took Xiling, and attacked and beheaded Geng Ye.
Xi crossed from Liupu, took Xiling, and attacked and beheaded Yu Ye.
The Chinese 庚業 is a graphic error for 庾業 (Yu Ye, cf. s0132c); the English should name Yu Ye.

On xinmao, Fangxing led the armies into battle; Prince of Jian'an Liu Xiuren also sent army commander Guo Jizhi, Infantry Commandant Du Youwen, Commandant of Palace Steeds Yuan Gongzu, Dragon-Coursing general Duan Furong of Jingzhao in Jidi, and thirty thousand others to join the fight; from dawn through noon they won a great victory and pursued the fugitives to Laoshan before returning.

On xinmao, Fangxing led the armies into battle; Prince of Jian'an Liu Xiuren also sent army commander Guo Jizhi, Infantry Commandant Du Youwen, Commandant of Garrison Cavalry Yuan Gongzu, Dragon-Coursing general Duan Furong of Jingzhao in Jidi, and thirty thousand others to join the fight; from dawn through noon they won a great victory and pursued the fugitives to Laoshan before returning.
屯騎校尉 is the Commandant of Garrison Cavalry.
On gengzi, Northern Wei appointed Wang Yuanhe of Shaanxi Grand Marshal.
On gengzi, Northern Wei appointed the Prince of Shanxi Yuan He Grand Commandant.
陝西王源賀 is Yuan He, Prince of Shanxi (源 is his surname; 王 is the princely title); 太尉 is Grand Commandant.
Staff Officer for the Central Troops Cai Na of the Champions, whose younger kinsmen were in Xiangyang, had them hung outside the walls whenever Hu fought;
Champion General Cai Na, Staff Officer for the Central Troops of the Minister over the Masses, whose younger kinsmen were in Xiangyang, had them hung outside the walls whenever Hu fought;
冠軍 is the title Champion General and 司徒 marks the Minister over the Masses' staff; "of the Champions" garbles both.
So many were ennobled for military merit that the printing blocks could not supply the commissions, and yellow paper began to be used.
So many were appointed to office for military merit that wooden commission tablets ran short, and yellow paper began to be used.
除官 means appointment to office, not ennoblement; 版 are wooden tablets of appointment, not printing blocks.

Wang Xuanmo, joint prefect of Pingyuan and Le'an, held Langye; Wang Xuanmiao, joint prefect of Qinghe and Guangchuan, held Panyang; Liu Chenmin, joint prefect of Gaoyang and Bohai, held Linji—all raised troops for Jiankang.

Wang Xuanmo, joint prefect of Pingyuan and Le'an, held Langye; Wang Xuanmiao, joint prefect of Qinghe and Guangchuan, held Panyang; Liu Chengmin, joint prefect of Gaoyang and Bohai, held Linji—all raised troops for Jiankang.
乘民: 乘 is read chéng (cf. s0306d Liu Chengmin).
Chenmin was a nephew of Liu Mizhi.
Chengmin was a nephew of Liu Mizhi.
Chenmin's younger cousin Bozong gathered the village clans, recovered Beihai, and marched toward Dongyang, seat of the Qingzhou government.
Chengmin's younger cousin Bozong gathered the village clans, recovered Beihai, and marched toward Dongyang, seat of the Qingzhou government.
Seng'ao, Xuanmo, Xuanmiao, and Chenmin combined to attack Dongyang; in every battle Wenxiu defeated them; they broke apart and rejoined more than ten times and ultimately could not take the city.
Seng'ao, Xuanmo, Xuanmiao, and Chengmin combined to attack Dongyang; in every battle Wenxiu defeated them; they broke apart and rejoined more than ten times and ultimately could not take the city.
Liu Mian wrote to Yin Yan as well and sent along a letter from Yan's nephew Yao, son of his brother Yuan.
Liu Mian wrote to Yin Yan as well and sent along a letter from Yan's nephew Miao, son of his brother Yuan.
When his food ran out his men broke apart; fleeing toward Leping, he was beheaded by Shen Lingsun's grandson Xiao Shuxiao.
When his food ran out his men broke apart; fleeing toward Leping, he was beheaded by Shen Lingsun's son Xiaoshu.
申令孫子孝叔 means Shen Lingsun's son (子) Xiaoshu (孝叔), not a grandson named Xiao Shuxiao.
Xue Andu's son Daozhi fled to Hefei and submitted to Pei Ji.
Xue Andu's son Daozhi fled to Hefei and submitted to Pei Jizhi.
裴季之 is Pei Jizhi; the final syllable was dropped.
Fu Lingyue fled to the Huai west; Martial Guard General Prince of Peijun Wang Guangzhi took him alive and sent him to Liu Mian.
Fu Lingyue fled to the Huai west; Martial Guard General Wang Guangzhi of Pei Commandery took him alive and sent him to Liu Mian.
沛郡 is Wang Guangzhi's native commandery; 王 is his surname, not a princely title.

Tian Yizhi led more than ten thousand barbarian warriors to besiege Yiyang; Deng Wan sent Sizhou inspector Pang Mengjiao with five thousand elite troops to relieve the city, and Yizhi broke camp and fled without fighting.

Tian Yizhi led more than ten thousand barbarian warriors to besiege Yiyang; Deng Wan sent Sizhou inspector Pang Mengqiu with five thousand elite troops to relieve the city, and Yizhi broke camp and fled without fighting.
龐孟虯: 虯 is read qiú.
Just then Pang Mengjiao marched to aid Yin Yan; Liu Mian's appeals for help grew desperate, and Prince of Jian'an Liu Xiuren meant to send Xingshi to his relief.
Just then Pang Mengqiu marched to aid Yin Yan; Liu Mian's appeals for help grew desperate, and Prince of Jian'an Liu Xiuren meant to send Xingshi to his relief.
龐孟虯: 虯 is read qiú.
Shen Youzhi said, "Mengjiao is only an ant swarm and can do nothing; send another commander with a few thousand horse and foot—that is enough to contain him.
Shen Youzhi said, "Mengqiu is only an ant swarm and can do nothing; send another commander with a few thousand horse and foot—that is enough to contain him.
Pang Mengjiao advanced to Yiyang; Liu Mian sent Lü Anguo and others to meet him at Liaotan and routed him; Mengjiao fled toward Yiyang.
Pang Mengqiu advanced to Yiyang; Liu Mian sent Lü Anguo and others to meet him at Liaotan and routed him; Mengqiu fled toward Yiyang.
龐孟虯: 虯 is read qiú.
Wang Xuemo's son Tanshan rose and seized Yiyang for Jiankang; Mengjiao fled and died among the barbarians.
Wang Xuanmo's son Tanshan rose and seized Yiyang for Jiankang; Mengqiu fled and died among the barbarians.
王玄謨 is Wang Xuanmo; 孟虯 is Mengqiu.

His retainer Huan Kang of Lanling carried off Ze's wife Lady Pei and sons Changmao and Ziliang into the hills; with Ze's kinsman Xiao Xizu and others they mustered more than a hundred fighting men, stormed the commandery, broke the jail, and freed Ze.

His retainer Huan Kang of Lanling carried off Ze's wife Lady Pei and sons Changmao and Ziliang into the hills; with Ze's kinsman Xiao Xinzu and others they mustered more than a hundred fighting men, stormed the commandery, broke the jail, and freed Ze.
蕭欣祖: 欣 is xīn.
Deng Wan appointed Central Guardian Army Yin Fu prefect of Yuzhang to oversee the five upper-stream commanderies against Liu Xi and his allies.
Deng Wan appointed Central Protector of the Army Yin Fu prefect of Yuzhang to oversee the five upper-stream commanderies against Liu Xi and his allies.
中護軍 is the office Central Protector of the Army.
In the eighth month, Huangfu Daolie and others, hearing of Pang Mengjiao's fall, all opened their gates and submitted.
In the eighth month, Huangfu Daolie and others, hearing of Pang Mengqiu's fall, all opened their gates and submitted.
龐孟虯: 虯 is read qiú.
Chen Qing reached Qianxi and made camp at Megan.
Chen Qing reached Qianxi and made camp at Meigen.
That same day Hu abandoned Yuan Yi and fled straight for Megan.
That same day Hu abandoned Yuan Yi and fled straight for Meigen.
Zi Xun stepped out with his blade and slew Wan.
His son Xun stepped out with his blade and slew Wan.
子洵 means Zhang Yue's son Xun, not a person named Zi Xun.

On gengzi Grand Minister Liu Xiuren reached Xunyang and dispatched Wu Xi and Zhang Xingshi to Jing, Shen Huaiming to Ying, Liu Liang and Pacifying-the-North general Zhang Jinger of Nanyang to Yong, Sun Chaozhi to Xiang, and Shen Siren and Ren Nongfu to Yuzhang to mop up the remaining rebels.

On gengzi Minister over the Masses Liu Xiuren reached Xunyang and dispatched Wu Xi and Zhang Xingshi to Jing, Shen Huaiming to Ying, Liu Liang and Pacifying-the-North general Zhang Jinger of Nanyang to Yong, Sun Chaozhi to Xiang, and Shen Siren and Ren Nongfu to Yuzhang to mop up the remaining rebels.
司徒 is the Minister over the Masses.
Grand Minister Liu Xiuren returned from Xunyang and told the emperor, "The Marquis of Songzi's brothers still live—that will not serve the throne's future. Deal with them soon."
Minister over the Masses Liu Xiuren returned from Xunyang and told the emperor, "The Marquis of Songzi's brothers still live—that will not serve the throne's future. Deal with them soon."
司徒 is the Minister over the Masses.
Princes of Anlu, Linhai, and Shaoling were all ordered to die; Liu Shun and the rest of the rebel faction in Jing were put to death.
Prince of Anlu Liu Zisui, Prince of Linhai Liu Zixu, and Prince of Shaoling Liu Ziwu were all ordered to die; Liu Shun and the rest of the rebel faction in Jing were put to death.
The Chinese names each prince (子綏, 子頊, 子無); the English dropped the personal names.

In winter, the tenth month, on yimao, Marquis of Songzi Liu Zifang, Princes of Yongjia, Shi'an, Huainan, Nanping, and Luling, Liu Ziqu, Liu Ziqi, Prince of Dongping Liu Zisi, and Liu Ziyue were all ordered to die, along with Northern Pacification adviser Lu Xiuzhi, secretariat attendant Lu Maozhi, Yanzhou inspector Liu Zhi, and secretariat gentleman Yan Long.

In winter, the tenth month, on yimao, Marquis of Songzi Liu Zifang, Prince of Yongjia Liu Ziren, Prince of Shi'an Liu Zizhen, Prince of Huainan Liu Zimeng, Prince of Nanping Liu Zichan, Prince of Luling Liu Ziyu, Liu Ziqu, Liu Ziqi, Prince of Dongping Liu Zisi, and Liu Ziyue were all ordered to die, along with Northern Pacification adviser Lu Xiuzhi, secretariat attendant Lu Maozhi, Yanzhou inspector Liu Zhi, and secretariat gentleman Yan Long.
The Chinese gives each prince's personal name (子仁, 子真, 子孟, 子產, 子輿); the English omitted them.

Xuzhou inspector Xue Andu, Yi inspector Xiao Huikai, Liangzhou inspector Liu Yuanku, Yanzhou inspector Bi Zhongjing, Yuzhang prefect Yin Fu, and Runan prefect Chang Zhenqi all sent envoys suing for peace.

Xuzhou inspector Xue Andu, Yi inspector Xiao Huikai, Liangzhou inspector Liu Yuanhu, Yanzhou inspector Bi Zhongjing, Yuzhang prefect Yin Fu, and Runan prefect Chang Zhenqi all sent envoys suing for peace.
柳元怙: 怙 is read hù.

Andu sent his son to Wei as a hostage; Wei sent Pacifying-the-East grand general Yu Yuan, a man of the Dai substitute line, Pacifying-the-East general Kong Bogong of Wei commandery, and others at the head of ten thousand cavalry along the eastern route to relieve Pengcheng;

Andu sent his son to Wei as a hostage; Wei sent Pacifying-the-East grand general Yu Yuan of Dai, Pacifying-the-East general Kong Bogong of Wei commandery, and others at the head of ten thousand cavalry along the eastern route to relieve Pengcheng;
代人 means a man of Dai (the Tuoba homeland), not a "substitute line".
Pacifying-the-West grand general Western River prince Shi and grand commander of Jing, Yu, and Southern Yongzhou Zhang Qiongqi marched by the western route to relieve Xuanhu.
Pacifying-the-West grand general Duke of Xihe Shi and grand commander of Jing, Yu, and Southern Yongzhou Zhang Qiongqi marched by the western route to relieve Xuanhu.
西河公 is the Duke of Xihe; 公 is duke, not prince.
Zhongjing's son Yuan Bin was in Jiankang and had already been put to death on another charge.
Zhongjing's son Yuanbin was in Jiankang and had already been put to death on another charge.
元賓 is the two-syllable given name Yuanbin of Bi Zhongjing's son.
Yan took the edict for a forgery by Liu Zhe and would not yield.
Yan took the edict for a forgery by Liu Mian and would not yield.
劉輒詐為之 means Liu (Mian) had arbitrarily forged it; 輒 is an adverb, not a name.
In the eleventh month, on renzi, Wei forces reached Xianqiu and Zhongjing sued for peace with Wei.
In the eleventh month, on renzi, Wei forces reached Xiaqiu and Zhongjing sued for peace with Wei.

unresolvedReferences.description: 其孫曇瓘 may mean Kong Ji's grandson Tanguan or a general Sun Tanguan (cf. 孫曇扞 in s0148c); treated as one person Sun Tanguan.
濟地頓生 before 京兆段佛榮 is unclear: it may be a further named officer (Dunsheng of Jidi) or a corrupt place phrase; no separate person created.
汝陰太守裴季 is taken as Pei Jizhi (裴季之, earlier southern Ruyin administrator at Hefei); the name appears truncated.
邵陵王子無: the personal name 無 may be a scribal corruption; recorded as Liu Ziwu per the packet.
